mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign shareholder (Company Registration Certificate or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national or state companies registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the shareholder's jurisdiction is party to the Hague Apostille Convention: notarize the certificate in the jurisdiction of issuance, then obtain an apostille from the designated competent authority of that jurisdiction; do not add consular legalization. If it is not an Apostille Convention party: notarize, legalize by the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize by the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that origin; do not add an apostille. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction (e.g., Companies Registry or Secretary of State office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuer is located in an Apostille Convention state: notarization followed by apostille from the competent authority of that state; Korean consular legalization is prohibited to be added. For non-member states: notarization, legalization by the foreign ministry of the issuer's state, then legalization by the Korean diplomatic or consular post covering that state; apostille is not added. These are exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney of the foreign shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Korean limited liability company and appointment of initial directors and representative director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or shareholders' meeting of the foreign shareholder; notarized by a competent notary in the issuer's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention jurisdictions: notarize the resolution, then apply to the designated competent authority for an apostille; do not submit to a Korean consulate for legalization. For non-Convention jurisdictions: notarize, legalize at the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate; no apostille is to be issued. The paths are mutually exclusive and must not be performed sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the foreign shareholder and draft Articles of Incorporation for the Korean Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder; draft Articles of Incorporation certified by the Korean formation attorney as conforming to the Commercial Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The foreign shareholder's articles are authenticated by notarization plus apostille if from an Apostille Convention state; if from a non-member state, notarization plus foreign-ministry legalization plus Korean consular legalization is applied. The Korean draft articles are notarized in Korea when required by banks. Apostille and consular legalization are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the foreign shareholder's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the shareholder's account; issued by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Where the bank is in an Apostille Convention jurisdiction: bank-signature notarization, then apostille from the competent authority of that jurisdiction; Korean consular legalization is not added. Where the bank is in a non-Convention jurisdiction: bank-signature notarization, origin foreign-ministry legalization, and Korean consular legalization; apostille is not added. The two authentication mechanisms are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening before onboarding and continuously throughout formation: (i) verify each UBO, director, shareholder, authorized signatory, and beneficial owner against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Non-SDN Sectoral Sanctions lists, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's designated persons list, and European Union sanctions lists; (ii) conduct Politically Exposed Person (PEP) screening using a risk-based approach covering international, domestic, and prominent public office holders, their families, and close associates; (iii) investigate adverse media, enforcement actions, regulatory disqualifications, and filings. Any positive match or PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-funds documentation, and, where necessary, rejection of the mandate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea (https://www.iros.go.kr) and the Korean registry name-clearance search available within the court's electronic commercial registration system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Korean commercial registration practice, the corporate name must be stated in Hangul (Korean alphabet). Foreign words and non-Korean company names are transliterated phonetically into Hangul and may include an English trade name in parentheses. The four-tier naming structure for a Yuhan Hoesa ordinarily comprises (1) distinctive trade name transliteration, (2) business-object description, (3) connectives/particles, and (4) the legal-form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' (limited liability company). Chinese ideographs (Hanja) and non-Hangul script may be used only as a supplementary interpretation, not as the operative registered name. The registry will not protect a name that is confusingly similar to an existing registered commercial name in the same line of business or to famous company names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant should first obtain the registry's written rejection or instructional reason (typically a service of correction order), correct the name and refile within the remaining registration period. If the rejection is substantive, the applicant may file a written name-registration objection or administrative appeal with the competent district court within the statutory objection period (generally 14 to 30 days) under the Commercial Registration Act, attaching the rejected search results, comparative name list, and legal arguments on similarity and legality. A further appeal is available to the High Court. If the applicant must preserve priority over a stronger competitor, simultaneously file a precautionary name reservation in an eligible business category.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or single-room mailing address is not permissible as the principal place of business for an ISIC 1050 UHT oat milk manufacturing and aseptic packaging company. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety food manufacturing facility license, municipal local tax registration, and commercial bank account opening all require a physical plant and warehousing site capable of statutory hygienic and production inspections. A registered office shared with an administrative service vendor may be allowed only as a supplemental corporate-address point, provided the actual production plant address is separately registered with the Korean tax authority and food authority. Banks will normally require a visit and proof of operational presence at the plant address, and may reject documentary-only virtual addresses for high-volume trade payments (SWIFT L/C, TT wires).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) MFDS pre-license facility inspection covering production line, aseptic packaging, CIP/SIP, water quality, and allergen management; (2) municipal quarantine and sanitation inspection; (3) national and local tax authority unannounced visit to verify place of actual management and VAT input invoices; (4) customs stamping and labelling inspection for export; (5) labor safety and fire prevention inspection. Quantified risk: high; probability of at least one unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of license issuance is estimated at 80-90% for a food-manufacturing plant, and 60-70% for tax purposes if the declared registered office differs from plant site. No free-zone or paper-office exemption applies under Korean local tax law.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter 4 on Limited Liability Companies (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 543 through 568, specifically Article 544 (contents of the Articles of Incorporation), Article 550 (capital and shares), Article 555 (full payment of capital contributions), Article 556 (share capital payment through designated financial institution), Article 562 (management organization), Article 563 (prohibition of interest-bearing dividends), Article 567 (statutory application of stock company registration provisions); together with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended), Articles 4, 5, and 6, for non-resident capital participation, and the Act on Registration of Real Estate, Court Dues, etc.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, National Court Administration, Supreme Court of Korea, with filings submitted electronically through the Internet Registration Office (IRO / i-registration portal) or in person at the Registry Office counter.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (법인설립등기신청서, romanized 'Beobin Seollip Deunggi Sincheongseo'), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the certificate of payment of the subscription price, the consent of each appointed director and auditor, and the registered office evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. There is no statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, the total subscription price of each issued share must be fully paid in before the incorporation registration (Article 555), and the full amount of the capital contribution must be deposited into a corporate-named provisional capital subscription receipt account at a commercial bank; no blocked escrow account is required by Korean law. For non-resident participants, the inbound contribution is settled through a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and the funds must be reported within twenty days of the share acquisition. The elected paid-in capital for this entity is KRW 100,000,000, represented by 200,000 shares of KRW 500 par value each.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE COMPANY'S INITIAL CORPORATE GOVERNING ORGAN, ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT THIS [DATE]. WHEREAS, Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), a commercial entity formed under the laws of the Republic of Korea, was organized under the Commercial Act with authorized paid-in capital of KRW 100,000,000 divided into 200,000 shares of KRW 500 par value each; and WHEREAS, the founding members and subscribers have irrevocably subscribed to all 200,000 shares and have fully paid the aggregate capital amount into the Company's provisional capital contribution receipt account maintained at a commercial bank; and WHEREAS, the Company's Articles of Incorporation empower the directors to transact all business of the Company and to establish, maintain, and close bank accounts; and WHEREAS, the Company intends to engage in the manufacture, aseptic UHT processing, and packaging of barista-format hydrolyzed oat milk, an activity requiring food safety, environmental, and civil defense licensing; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED, effective as of the date of the Company's formation registration, as follows: 1. Capital Subscription and Allotment. The subscription of 200,000 shares at par value of KRW 500 each, representing KRW 100,000,000 in aggregate, and the full payment of the same are ratified, confirmed, and accepted. The directors are directed to record such shares in the corporate shareholder register and to issue share certificates evidencing the same to the members. 2. Adoption of Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be and is hereby established at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, Seoul, Republic of Korea, until lawfully changed by subsequent resolution. The directors are authorized to file the registration of the registered office with the competent Registry Office and to receive all legal service of process at such address. 3. Banking Authorization. The Company's primary banking relationship is hereby established with the bank designated by the Chief Executive Officer. The Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer are authorized, acting jointly for transactions exceeding KRW 50,000,000 and individually for ordinary-course transactions, to open and close corporate operating and foreign currency accounts; to execute account application forms, officer certificates, and beneficial ownership declarations; to sign checks, promissory notes, SWIFT/LC instructions, and TT wire orders; and to terminate such accounts when necessary. All signatory instruments shall be supported by a certified corporate seal certificate. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. [Name, passport number, nationality] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director; [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer with responsibility for tax filings, corporate books, and AML/CFT remediation; and [Name] is appointed Auditor (gamsa) in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and Chapter 4 of the Commercial Act. 5. Governance and Compliance. The officers are directed to prepare and retain statutory minutes, maintain the corporate seal, obtain the Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service within twenty days of incorporation, and complete all foreign investment notifications, food manufacturing licensing, and factory safety permits described in the Stage 2 formation SOP. 6. Effective Date. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption and may be executed in counterparts. ADOPTED this [day] day of [month], [year], in Seoul, Republic of Korea. Signed: _______, Chief Executive Officer; _______, Chief Financial Officer; _______, Auditor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Notarization and Capital Contribution Pay-In
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public having jurisdiction in Seoul and the designated commercial bank where the provisional capital subscription receipt account is opened.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language, accurately reciting the corporate name, registered office address, corporate objects covering the manufacture of aseptic barista-format hydrolyzed oat milk, the total authorized capital of KRW 100,000,000, the par value per share, and the names of the initial directors and auditor. Submit the draft Articles for notarization, and cause each promoter to appear before the notary to authenticate identity and signature. Following notarization, open a provisional capital subscription receipt account in the Company's name at a licensed commercial bank, and arrange for each subscriber to remit the full subscription amount into that account. Obtain from the bank a certificate of deposit of the total subscription price confirming full contribution, as this certificate is an indispensable attachment to the subsequent court registration application.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original certified copies)
Passport or national ID copies of each promoter and subscribing member
Power of attorney executed in favor of the local filing counsel or representative
Pro-Forma First Board Resolution appointing officers and approving the capital subscription
Bank certificate of deposit confirming full payment of the subscription price
Registered office evidence, including lease agreement or landlord's written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the Articles with a query or correction note, convene a supplementary meeting of promoters to approve the amended text, re-notarize the corrected Articles, and re-submit within five business days; if the bank declines to issue the certificate of deposit due to KYC deficiencies, furnish corrected seal certificates and beneficial ownership documents and request expedited re-issuance from the same bank or substitute another licensed commercial bank without delaying the court filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, National Court Administration, Supreme Court of Korea, submitted electronically through the Internet Registration Office (IRO).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation of the Limited Liability Company with the Registry Court within fourteen days of the notarization of the Articles and completion of the capital contribution pay-in. Submit the application through the IRO electronic portal or in person at the Registry counter, attaching the notarized Articles, the bank certificate of deposit, the signed consent of each director and auditor, and the registered office evidence. Pay electronically the registration tax of 0.4% of the paid-in capital, together with the 20% education surtax and court stamp duty. The examiner will verify statutory compliance, including the complete payment of capital, the lawful designation of the representative director and auditor, and the absence of restricted business objects. Upon approval, the court issues the certified Certificate of Registered Matters, and the Company acquires juridical personality.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation (statutory form completed and signed)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original)
Bank certificate of deposit of the full subscription price
Written consent to appointment of each director and auditor
Certificate or supporting evidence of the registered office (lease registration excerpt or landlord consent)
Corporate seal declaration and specimen seal certificate
Power of attorney for the filing counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplemental request or correction order, cure each identified defect within the statutory period, normally two weeks, by uploading the corrected documents through the IRO and paying any incremental fees; if the application is suspended because the Articles contain a prohibited business object, adopt an amended resolution of the promoters, re-notarize the revised Articles, and file a new application with a cover letter explaining the amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Tax Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Head of the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, National Tax Service, acting through the HomeTX electronic tax portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days of the issuance of the Certificate of Registered Matters, submit the business registration application (business operator registration) to the competent District Tax Office, or file electronically through the HomeTX portal. Present the corporate registration certificate, the corporate seal certificate, and the lease or proof of the registered office to obtain the Business Registration Certificate. Complete the registration of the corporate income tax account, value-added tax registration, and the payroll withholding tax accounts for employees. Select the correct business category code in the Korean Standard Industrial Classification corresponding to the manufacture of grain and plant-based liquid beverages consistent with ISIC 1050, and designate the responsible tax representative. The Business Registration Certificate is a prerequisite to the opening of an operating bank account and the filing of all subsequent food and environmental license applications.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters issued by the Registry Court
Business registration application form (form prescribed by the National Tax Service)
Corporate seal certificate and specimen seal declaration
Registered office lease agreement and building owner identification
First Board Resolution appointing the tax representative
Bank account certificate or provisional capital account statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the District Tax Office returns the application for want of a physical place of business, submit the floor plan, utility bills, and a written confirmation from the building owner; if the business category is questioned, amend the classification to the precise Korean Standard Industrial Classification subclass for plant-based beverage manufacturing and re-submit through HomeTX, paying any applicable correction surcharge within the response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report Under FIPA and Activation of Operating Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest KOREA, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and the designated foreign exchange bank maintaining the Company's operating account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after any non-resident member acquires shares, file the foreign investment report under Article 6 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with the designated foreign exchange bank or with KOTRA. The report must state the identity of the foreign investor, the corporate name of the domestic company, the business scope pertaining to aseptic UHT oat milk manufacturing, the number and par value of acquired shares, the total investment amount, and the inbound remittance channel. Upon acceptance, obtain the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, which confers foreign investor protection and eligibility for tax incentives. Simultaneously, present the complete corporate dossier to the bank's compliance department, including the corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, notarized passport copies, and the First Board Resolution authorizing the signatories, to activate the operating account with SWIFT/LC and TT wire capabilities.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment report form prescribed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
Certificate of Registered Matters and Business Registration Certificate
Passport or national ID of each foreign shareholder and beneficial owner
Beneficial ownership declaration and AML/KYC compliance questionnaire
Bank remittance slip or certificate of foreign currency inward remittance
Foreign Investment Registration Certificate (issued after report acceptance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's compliance unit issues a request for further information, respond in the prescribed secure channel within the stated deadline and provide any missing corporate or beneficial ownership evidence; if the foreign investment report is declined, re-file with KOTRA through its Invest KOREA one-stop service or correct the report form and submit to an alternative designated foreign exchange bank, ensuring that the twenty-day statutory deadline is observed and an administrative extension is requested where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Safety, Environmental, and Civil Defense Facility Licensing for the UHT Plant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) regional office, Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) under the Ministry of Employment and Labor, the municipal fire safety and civil defense authority, and the local environmental permitting office of the Ministry of Environment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to commencing commercial production, obtain the Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License under Article 36 of the Food Sanitation Act by filing the application with the MFDS regional office having jurisdiction over the factory. Submit the facility layout, aseptic UHT line specifications, homogenizer and aseptic filler drawings, CIP/SIP system design, water quality test reports, and the HACCP prerequisite program, and pass the on-site inspection verifying thermal processing parameters, aseptic filling environment, allergen control, and packaging material compliance. In parallel, file the wastewater discharge facility report under Article 33 of the Water Environment Conservation Act with the municipal environmental authority, submit the air emission facility report for the package boiler, and complete the firefighting system design review and subsequent completion inspection under the Firefighting Facilities Installation and Maintenance Act. Obtain the building occupancy approval, the Civil Defense simple shelter designation where the floor area exceeds 5,000 m², and the KOSHA workplace safety approval under Article 36 of the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including the risk assessment for pressure vessels, steam boiler, ammonia refrigeration, confined spaces, and chemical use.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Registered Matters
Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License application form approved by MFDS
Factory site plan, floor plan, architectural drawings, and mechanical and electrical drawings
Specification sheets for the UHT sterilizer, aseptic filler, homogenizer, and CIP/SIP system
Potable water quality analysis report
HACCP implementation plan and prerequisite program documentation
Wastewater discharge facility report and effluent prediction statement
Air emission facility report for the boiler
Building occupancy permit, fire safety design approval, and firefighting facility completion certificate
Occupational safety and health management plan and KOSHA registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS issues a correction order after inspection, remediate each non-conformity such as sanitizer application, air filtration, drainage, or record-keeping within the statutory grace period of fifteen to thirty days and apply for re-inspection; if the environmental agency rejects the wastewater report, submit the revised pre-treatment system design and recalculated effluent quality data; if the fire authority withholds the completion certificate, install the specified fire doors, sprinklers, alarms, and emergency lighting and request a supplemental inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Food Safety Policy Bureau and its regional (city/provincial) offices; Korea Agency of HACCP Accreditation and Management for HACCP certification; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) under the Ministry of Employment and Labor; the municipal fire safety and civil defense department; and the Ministry of Environment together with the local environmental permitting office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License under Article 36(1) of the Food Sanitation Act, together with the aseptic UHT manufacturing facility conformity certificate under the MFDS Food Code and the Standards of Manufacturing and Processing of Food; HACCP Certification (recommended); and the wastewater discharge facility and air emission facility registrations under the relevant environmental statutes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (ME), Korea Environment Corporation, and the relevant municipal environmental permitting office, supported by the Korea Environmental Industry and Technology Institute (KEITI).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration and Wastewater Discharge Facility Report tier; a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report under the Act on Assessment of Environmental Impacts is not required for a UHT plant of this scale unless the total development area is 100,000 m² or greater or the facility is sited within an environmental preservation district, water-source protection zone, or other sensitive buffer area, in which case a Small-Scale (Preliminary) Environmental Impact Review applies; otherwise, the facility is subject to wastewater discharge facility registration under Article 33 of the Water Environment Conservation Act and air emission facility reporting under the Clean Air Conservation Act for the package boiler.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Effluent discharged to a receiving water body: BOD5 not exceeding 10 mg/L, COD (Mn) not exceeding 40 mg/L, TOC not exceeding 20 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 10 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 20 mg/L, total phosphorus not exceeding 2 mg/L, total coliforms not exceeding 3,000 MPN/100 mL, and pH in the range of 5.8 to 8.6; where pre-treated effluent is discharged into a public wastewater treatment system, BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, TOC not exceeding 30 mg/L, and suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, all per the Water Environment Conservation Act Enforcement Rules. Air emissions from the boiler: particulate matter not exceeding 30 mg/Sm³, nitrogen oxides not exceeding 40 ppm, and sulfur oxides not exceeding 4 ppm per the Clean Air Conservation Act; boundary odor intensity maintained at or below 15 dilution units at the nearest residential-sensitive receptor. Hazardous CIP and caustic residues, cleaning sludge, and rejected product waste must be consigned to licensed waste handlers through the electronic waste manifest system, and boundary noise in an industrial zone is limited to 65 dB(A) during the daytime and 55 dB(A) at night.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Firefighting Systems Completion Inspection Certificate including automatic fire alarm, sprinkler, and portable extinguisher equipment, preceded by a fire safety design review approval under the Firefighting Facilities Installation and Maintenance Act; building occupancy approval under the Building Act; a Civil Defense simple shelter designation or evacuation facility plan issued by the local government where the total factory floor area exceeds 5,000 m²; pressure vessel and steam boiler operating permits; prior occupational safety approval from the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency under Article 36 of the Occupational Safety and Health Act covering the UHT aseptic line, CIP chemical storage, confined spaces, electrical grounding, and emergency response; an electrical installation inspection by the Korea Electrical Safety Corporation; and a workplace environment measurement report for noise, heat stress, and food dust filed with KOSHA.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (http://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa in South Korea must first complete court registration under the Korean Commercial Act at the local district court registry, then file an Application for Business Registration with the competent NTS district tax office (or through HomeTax) within 20 days from the commencement of business. Supporting documents include the certificate of incorporation, registered articles of incorporation, registered corporate seal or authenticated signature of the representative, place-of-business lease or ownership documentation, and, if applicable, the foreign investment report certificate issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The NTS then issues the entity's 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as both the national Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the Value-Added Tax (VAT) identification number for the enterprise. For a foreign corporation with no domestic place of business, the entity must appoint a domestic tax representative and complete non-resident business registration with the NTS through HomeTax; the NTS will assign a separate non-resident taxpayer identification reference for Korean tax return, withholding, and VAT compliance purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or general pass-through classification for a Yuhan Hoesa. A domestic group that satisfies the statutory wholly-owned domestic subsidiary conditions may elect consolidated (group) corporation tax treatment under the Corporate Tax Act; however, hybrid mismatch election mechanisms are not available and anti-hybrid rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act apply to disallow inappropriate deduction/non-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold exists. Every business operator that supplies goods or services in Korea is mandatorily required to register for VAT from the first taxable supply, i.e., effective threshold KRW 0. A KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover threshold applies only for classification as a simplified taxable person and the associated simplified VAT calculation; it does not exempt a business from registration under the VAT Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses, including corporations, must issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoices) through the NTS HomeTax system or an NTS-approved e-invoice ASP service provider, and the invoice data is transmitted to the NTS in real time upon issuance. Mandatory e-invoice data fields include the issuer and recipient business registration numbers, supply date, item description, taxable amount, VAT amount, and unique invoice serial number. The NTS performs real-time schema validation, applies anti-fraud digital verification and automated cross-checks between purchase and sales ledgers, and pre-fills VAT return data for taxpayers. A paper tax invoice generally cannot support an input VAT credit for a business-to-business purchase that is subject to mandatory e-invoicing; the electronic record must be retrievable in the HomeTax system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods are zero-rated when the goods are physically moved out of the Republic of Korea and the export is evidenced by an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service. A business may also zero-rate qualifying offshore services supplied to a non-resident for use outside Korea, provided the service contract, recipient's place of residence or establishment, and actual place of use are objectively documented. For the manufacture and export of UHT oat milk, the exporter must maintain full evidence that the goods were exported, the proceeds were collected in foreign currency or as agreed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and the commercial benefit was received by a non-resident overseas buyer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration accepted through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic clearance system
Bill of Lading (B/L) or air waybill evidencing export shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Korean foreign exchange receipt confirmation evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Purchase order or underlying export sales contract with the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and the Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export zero-rating claims and require production of all export and foreign-exchange documentation. If the statutory fulfillment evidence is inadequate or the export is found to be fabricated, the zero-rating is reversed and the NTS reassesses the 10% VAT on the unsubstantiated export supply, plus interest and additional penalty tax. Fraudulent or intentional underpayment claims and false export declarations may expose the entity to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment or fines, and to customs-related penalties under the Customs Act. The export proceeds must be settled and repatriated within 180 days of the export declaration; non-repatriation without an approved extension may cause the NTS or the Bank of Korea to treat the export as unjustified, with retrospective VAT clawback and exchange-control penalties. The general statute of limitations for national tax reassessment is five years, but it extends to ten years where the taxpayer filed fraudulently or omitted the transaction through false or fake documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), acting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalised current account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account settlements, including trade payments, service fees and dividend disbursements, are generally permitted without prior approval when executed via a registered foreign exchange bank using prescribed settlement methods. Capital account movements are more controlled: inward foreign direct investment requires a notification through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and subsequent capital transactions must be reported to the Bank of Korea through the designated foreign exchange bank. Export proceeds are not subject to a mandatory percentage surrender obligation; however, they must be received within the statutory receipt term, typically one year from the export declaration date, and must be settled through a Korean foreign exchange bank or maintained in a domestic foreign currency account. Profit remittance is structurally permitted for a foreign-invested entity once corporate taxes are filed and paid, but the bank will require evidence of the foreign investment declaration, audited financial statements, tax payment certificates and a board resolution approving the dividend. Practical hurdles include prolonged documentary verification, harmonised transaction code reporting, and anti-money laundering review of the ultimate beneficial owner.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency proceeds must be received by the Korean exporter via a domestic foreign exchange bank within one year from the date of export declaration, with extension possible only under narrowly defined circumstances reported to the Bank of Korea. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio; the entity may retain export receipts in a foreign currency demand deposit account or convert them to Korean won at market rates, but the bank must confirm the export customs declaration, invoice, shipping documents and packing list before settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Korean Won Current Account
Comprehensive Corporate Foreign Currency and Won Settlement Account
Trade Settlement, Letter of Credit and Foreign Currency Account
Foreign Direct Investment Capital Account / Operational Currency Account
SME Manufacturing Treasury Account and Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Account
Agri-Food Trade Settlement Account and Agricultural Commodity Import Payment Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. An offshore digital EMI is not a permitted substitute for a Korean foreign exchange bank. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act require any provider of corporate payment and clearing services in Korean won to hold a valid domestic licence. No overseas EMI can lawfully open a settlement account, generate Korean won clearing references, or submit Bank of Korea BOP reporting. Therefore, the Yuhan Hoesa treasury structure must pivot on a domestic Tier 1 commercial bank, with any offshore EMI used only as a non-routing ancillary tool, if at all.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Korean LLC, statutory directors are normally required to attend the bank branch in person to verify identity and complete the KYC interview. Remote opening via consular proxy is not a general right; a foreign director may appoint an in-country representative or co-director under a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, but the bank compliance officer may still require a video interview or an in-person visit before account activation. Fully digital onboarding is generally unavailable for a foreign-owned manufacturing entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous beneficial ownership structure for a Korean LLC owned by non-residents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, statutory representative appointment resolution, foreign investor registration certificate if applicable, notarised and consularised certificate of incumbency for each shareholder, government-issued identification, proof of address, ultimate beneficial owner declaration covering any 25% or more indirect interest, full organisational chart, and proof of the legal source of the initial paid-in capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering suspicion due to agricultural commodity flows involving oat raw materials and packaging supplies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete supply chain contracts, purchase orders, commercial invoices, export and import customs declarations, bills of lading, phytosanitary certificates, insurance certificates, UHT production batch records, oat milk formula specifications, packaging material reconciliation files, and bank-to-bank correspondence proving the physical movement of goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected cross-border wire flows and mismatched foreign exchange purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy manual, board-approved funding plan with monthly cash flow forecast, foreign exchange purpose code for each transaction covering dividend, royalty, trade settlement and capital contribution, underlying trade or investment contracts, and a written explanation for any split payments, round-tripped flows or third-party counter-party involvement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential tax evasion or unlawful profit extraction through inflated management fees, royalties or intra-group charges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing documentation under Korean tax rules, full trial balance, arm's length benchmark or local file, board minutes approving each fee or royalty, FATCA and CRS self-certification for all shareholders, shareholder tax residency declarations, evidence of withholding tax payment to the National Tax Service, and correlation of service fees to actual commercial activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be routed through a Korean foreign exchange bank using a Foreign Investment Promotion Act declaration filed prior to remittance. The wire should be an SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank in cleared funds, clearly referencing the foreign investment notification registration number and the Bank of Korea assigned direct investment purpose code for capital contribution. After receipt, the bank will issue a foreign exchange purchase and sale confirmation and capital verification; the company must then complete the foreign-invested enterprise registration through KOTRA or the local Integrated Support Center. Do not commingle loan proceeds, personal funds or third-party payments into the capital injection wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire settlement of raw oat imports, packaging films, UHT packaging cartons and other input purchases. Commercial letters of credit, both sight and usance, are preferred for high-value equipment imports and are to be issued by the domestic Tier 1 bank with standard ICC UCP 600 terms. Documentary collections may be used for low-risk, low-value shipments, but the bank must verify the underlying export or import declaration and maintain accurate balance-of-payments reporting for each outward remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward outright contracts are permissible for matched export and import trade cash flows when executed with a designated Korean foreign exchange bank and supported by documented underlying trade exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are available to Korean corporates only for hedging non-trade emerging-market currency exposure and require Bank of Korea reporting where the Korean won leg is settled separately; pure speculative Korean won NDFs are restricted.

Cross-currency swaps are permitted for balance-sheet hedging of EUR, USD and KRW exposures, limited to the underlying current or capital account transaction, subject to bank credit approval and a board-approved risk policy.

European-style FX options are permissible as premium-covered hedging tools when the maturity aligns with documented trade cash flows and the notional does not exceed the underlying receivable or payable exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Members and approval of annual financial statements for the Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external registry filing; the resolution and authenticated minutes are maintained at the registered head office and are subject to inspection by the National Tax Service, Financial Supervisory Service, or a court upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary meeting or to prepare and retain the minutes and financial statements may expose the directors and members to administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Korean Commercial Act; unauthorized dividends may be voidable and subject to claw-back from knowingly receiving members; persistent deadlock may ultimately lead to a court-ordered dissolution of the limited company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and external audit report filing (statutory external audit deliverable under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer system, with information notified to the Securities and Futures Commission of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the ordinary general meeting of members approves the financial statements; if no approval meeting is held, the filing is enforced no later than two weeks after the statutory approval deadline, resulting in an outer date of April 15 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 30,000,000 under the External Audit Act; the company may be classified as an audit-managed entity requiring semi-annual additional reports; the National Tax Service may disregard unaudited or insufficiently audited financial statements and impose corporate tax penalties and documentary evidence penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax final return and local income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic system, with the local income tax component reported to the competent local government via the national integrated tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the close of the fiscal year; where the return is prepared and signed by a certified Korean tax accountant or CPA and filed electronically, the extended deadline is April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the unpaid corporate tax; under-reporting or over-deduction triggers additional tax of 10 percent or 20 percent of the under-reported amount depending on the level of willfulness; overdue tax accrues interest at 0.022 percent per day, approximately 8.03 percent per annum; after a 30-day delinquency notice, the National Tax Service may seize business assets and cancel the business registration, and prolonged non-filing with no business activity can result in court-led compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment maintenance or change report for the foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, operational delegation to KOTRA and the Korea Investment Ombudsman
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standing annual filing; a written report must be submitted within 30 days after any triggering event, including transfer of membership interests, change of foreign investor identity or nationality, capital increase or decrease, change of business scope, relocation of head office, or dissolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the event-based report may subject the company and foreign investor to criminal fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and may disqualify the company from foreign-invested enterprise tax incentives and legal protections; it does not by itself trigger administrative strike-off but can impair bank payment rails such as SWIFT documentary credits and TT wires during KYC/AML review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register reconciliation and beneficial ownership confirmation, including the Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages and minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory registers are maintained on-site at the registered head office and must be produced to the National Tax Service, Financial Supervisory Service, Financial Intelligence Unit, court, or any authorized supervisory agency upon lawful demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously maintained; mandatory internal reconciliation must be completed no later than the date of the ordinary general meeting of members, and any transfer of a membership interest or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected in the statutory registers within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or incomplete statutory registers may attract administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Korean Commercial Act; in an AML examination context, inaccurate beneficial ownership records may trigger Financial Intelligence Unit enforcement actions, enhance banking due diligence, and interrupt the opening or continuation of transaction banking relationships.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a private Korean Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor when total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000, approximately USD 8,900,000 at a KRW 1,350/USD exchange rate. Mandatory external audit also applies if the entity is a listed or publicly traded company regardless of asset size, or if the Securities and Futures Commission designates the company as subject to external audit by reason of public interest, industry significance, investor protection, or systemic risk. For a private LLC that does not exceed the KRW 12 billion asset threshold, there is no standalone revenue or headcount trigger for a statutory external audit under Korean law; however, the company must still prepare accurate financial statements under the applicable accounting framework and maintain its statutory books and registers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS, being Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, applies to listed companies and any company required to use K-IFRS by regulation; non-listed private companies, including a Yuhan Hoesa, may apply K-GAAP, the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, which are aligned with IFRS. All audits of Korean statutory-purpose financial statements must be conducted in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants, and financial statements must be expressed in Korean won.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa has no separate annual UBO filing requirement to a company registry, but it must file a change report with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy/KOTRA within 30 days of any change in foreign shareholding, nationality, capital, or status. Domestically, the company must maintain a current and accurate Register of Members, and beneficial ownership information must be reconciled and confirmed at each ordinary members' meeting or through a documented internal annual confirmation performed no later than the date of that meeting. While no annual UBO return is submitted to a public authority for a non-regulated private LLC, the beneficial ownership data must be made immediately available to regulated financial institutions for KYC/AML purposes and to the Financial Intelligence Unit or competent court upon lawful request. Any shareholding transfer or indirect ownership change must be recorded in the statutory register and, where foreign-invested status is affected, reported within the 30-day statutory window.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 per annum for a Seoul or Busan registered office address with professional company secretarial and registered-agent-style support; USD 800 to USD 2,000 per annum for mail-forwarding and address-only services; annual corporate secretarial retainer for a foreign-owned operating LLC typically ranges from USD 2,500 to USD 6,000 including statutory register maintenance and meeting coordination.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 to USD 45,000 for a mid-sized UHT plant-based beverage manufacturing company near the statutory audit threshold; USD 45,000 to USD 120,000 for a more complex operation with significant revenue, intercompany transactions, or group consolidated reporting under K-IFRS; actual fees fluctuate with engagement hours, transaction volume, and the auditor's KICPA-approved fee schedule.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% national CIT (KRW 20 billion+ bracket) plus 10% local income tax surcharge, producing an aggregate headline rate of 24.2%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit up to 30% of qualifying expenditures and patent box equivalent for specialized manufacturing technology; investment tax credits for automated UHT aseptic production lines and clean-energy facilities; statutory tax reductions for foreign-invested high-tech enterprises in free economic zones; venture SME tax holiday for eligible small- and medium-sized enterprises

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Form 1) plus attached annex schedules, electronically filed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax portal under the Corporate Tax Act
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with semi-annual preliminary tax returns for companies with prior-year taxable income)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year filers), extendable by one month with a qualified tax accountant review certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: name, representative, business registration number, corporate address, fiscal year, and industry code (ISIC 1050 - Manufacturer of aseptic oat milk beverages)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Register as a non-resident domestic place of business (UPE) with the Korean branch registration number; designate a Korean resident tax agent and state the head office address in the foreign country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue (total sales of packaged UHT aseptic oat milk, co-packaging services, and by-products)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Korean-source gross income attributable to the Korean UHT plant. Exclude off-shore sales without source nexus, but include domestic delivery, FOB contracts discharging in Korea, and direct online B2B/B2C Korean consumer sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of Sales (raw oat inputs, packaging materials, utility costs, direct labor) and Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's length recharges for head-office allocations and foreign parent service charges; no profit-stripping via excessive royalties or inflated management fees; add back non-deductible intercompany interest exceeding statutory thin-capitalization limits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income legal adjustments: book income reconciled to tax base through reserves, non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, and loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible items must include excessive related-party entertainment, fines, penalties, and tax paid to foreign jurisdictions without treaty basket; claim only Korean statutory allowable depreciation for UHT equipment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, withholding tax credits, and double tax treaty relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident Korean UPE may claim treaty credits for foreign parent taxes only if prohibited by treaty; attach DTA relief forms, submit Tax Residency Certificate of beneficial owner, and evidence of no permanent establishment beyond the declared Korean place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax, local income tax surcharge, and provisional payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate national CIT plus 10% local surcharge; for outbound dividends paid by a Korean LLC to the non-resident shareholder, deny deduction and apply the withholding tax at the treaty rate only after proper DTA filing through the investing company's local filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of unpaid corporate tax; non-payment daily surcharge of 0.025% per day; unfaithful declaration penalty of 20% (understated tax) and 40% for fraudulent statements; criminal tax evasion sanction under the Framework Act on National Taxes of imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 50 million, jointly with the local surcharge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national dividend withholding for non-residents plus 10% local income tax surcharge on that withholding, resulting in an aggregate 22% non-resident dividend WHT rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the DTA-reduced dividend rate, the non-resident recipient must file an application for treaty relief with the Korean payer before remittance, provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority covering the dividend payment date, complete a Korean Schedule of DTA Withholding, prove beneficial ownership (no back-to-back arrangement or conduit), and provide a signed BOI form; if the treaty rate was applied provisionally, the excess can be reclaimed through a formal NTS refund application within three years from the statutory tax payment date
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound interest WHT 20% national plus 10% local surcharge (aggregate 22%), reduced by treaties commonly to 10% or 15%; outbound royalty WHT 20% national plus 10% local surcharge (aggregate 22%), reduced by treaties commonly to 10% or 15%, subject to beneficial-ownership and anti-royalty-stripping rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border intercompany transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion in the fiscal year trigger mandatory Local File preparation and KRW 50 billion for the Master File; in all cases a simplified intercompany transaction disclosure schedule must be attached to the corporate tax return, including arm's length range and selection methodology
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korean tax law and the OECD BEPS-aligned International Tax Adjustment Act apply a substance-over-form doctrine: the UHT plant must demonstrate physical premises, qualified staffing, purchase and production operational control (CIGA), risk incidence, and decision-making in Korea. An offshore shell or pass-through headquarters with no Korean management board, payroll, or warehouse has no economic substance and the entity can be disregarded for Korean corporate income tax and treaty purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Korean UHT oat milk sales revenue from the CIT return, forging purchase invoices for oat raw materials, or channeling profits through a sham nominee distributor controlled by the non-resident parent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes and Corporate Tax Act, a fraudulent under-declaration triggers an additional 40% unfaithful-return penalty, daily non-payment surcharge, immediate assessment of evaded tax plus local surcharge, and criminal reference to the public prosecutor's office; the penalty tax can equal or exceed the original liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts and NTS pierce the corporate veil if the LLC was used as a sham or instrument of tax fraud: directors, including foreign shadow directors, become jointly and severally liable for the shortfall, property is subject to attachment without reserve, personal bank accounts are frozen, departure from Korea is banned (travel blacklisting), and criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years may be imposed for each fraudulent return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the intercompany price for oat grain, aseptic carton stock, and equipment rental unrelated to market benchmarks, or paying management fees and royalty charges to the corporate parent above the arm's length price without demonstrating actual services or IP contribution, thereby eroding the Korean tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may re-audit, redetermine the arm's length income under the International Tax Adjustment Act, impose a 20% underreporting penalty on the adjusted excessive expense, apply a 0.75% monthly interest on the deficiency, and deny the deduction; if the adjustment is intentional, the penalty rises to 40% and the CFC/anti-avoidance provisions apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the intercompany pricing policy and instructed the excessive remittance face joint and several civil liability for the adjusted corporation tax, interest and penalties, are personally disqualified from serving in board roles, have personal assets attached in the NTS collection process, and can be prosecuted for fiscal fraud with imprisonment from 1 to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC operates as a shell with no management, no substantive employees, no operative plant control, and no core income-generating activities, while the foreign parent services a dividend or royalty out of Korea by claiming treaty benefits that presuppose real economic substance; the entity is deliberately used as a conduit to route income into a low-tax or no-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Corporate Tax Act and International Tax Adjustment Act, tax authorities disregard the shell entity, deny treaty benefits under the domestic GAAR and principal-purpose test, join the parent and the LLC as a single taxpayer, reassess all outbound distributions as Korean-source constructive dividends, and impose a 40% fraud penalty plus local surcharge and daily overdue interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell are jointly liable for the reassessed corporate tax and penalties because the corporate form was a sham, personal travel is restricted by the NTS blacklist, the director's personal property is civilly seized to satisfy the corporate debt, and the misconduct is classified under embezzlement and tax fraud rules with imprisonment terms up to 5 years and/or criminal fines of up to KRW 50 million.
